target.title: fix: reject Telegram topic sessions_send targets
target.body:
Closes #99835

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users calling `sessions_send` with a Telegram topic session key could dispatch an inter-agent run against the topic child session instead of getting the existing thread-session rejection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct-target guard now uses the full session thread parser, so loaded/plugin-owned session conversation metadata is considered before dispatch. This keeps Telegram topic handling at the channel/plugin session-key boundary rather than adding Telegram-specific `:topic:` parsing to the generic core suffix parser.

Related PR #99844 covers the same issue by teaching the generic suffix parser about `:topic:`. This PR instead follows the issue review's requested fix shape: reuse the plugin-owned lightweight session-key resolver path for `sessions_send`.

## User Impact

Telegram topic session targets now receive the same parent-session guidance as other thread child sessions. The tool rejects before queueing or dispatching an agent run, so users avoid accidental nested work in the topic child context.

## Evidence

- Current head proved: `c183205bea115e3d4cffe17b661b09fb75735f21`.
- Claim proved: `sessions_send` rejects a Telegram topic session target before gateway dispatch when the channel session resolver classifies `:topic:` as a threaded child conversation.
- Source path checked:
  - `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts:515` calls `parseSessionThreadInfo(resolvedKey).threadId` before dispatch and returns the existing `sessions_send cannot target a thread session...` error when a child thread/topic is detected.
  - `src/config/sessions/thread-info.ts` delegates `parseSessionThreadInfo(...)` to the plugin-aware session conversation resolver, while the fast loaded-only helper remains separate.
  - `src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts:58` adds a Telegram resolver stub that maps `agent:main:telegram:group:-100123:topic:77` to base conversation `-100123` plus `threadId: "77"`.
  - `src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts:1021` asserts the topic target returns `status: "error"`, includes `cannot target a thread session`, and `callGatewayMock` is not called.
- Focused regression run on this head:

```text
node_modules\.bin\vitest.cmd run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-tools.config.ts src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts --reporter=verbose -t "rejects Telegram topic session targets"

PASS |agents-tools| src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts > sessions_send gating > rejects Telegram topic session targets before dispatching an agent run 17ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  1 passed | 43 skipped (44)
```

- File-level regression run on this head:

```text
node_modules\.bin\vitest.cmd run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-tools.config.ts src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts --reporter=verbose

PASS |agents-tools| src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts > sessions_send gating > rejects direct thread session targets before dispatching an agent run
PASS |agents-tools| src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts > sessions_send gating > rejects Telegram topic session targets before dispatching an agent run
PASS |agents-tools| src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts > sessions_send gating > rejects label targets that resolve to canonical thread sessions
PASS |agents-tools| src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts > sessions_send gating > does not disclose a resolved thread session key from a sessionId target
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  44 passed (44)
```

- Hygiene: `git diff --check` passed.
- CI proof on current PR head: `Real behavior proof` passed at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28698259016/job/85111951915.
- Review: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` reported `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`.
- Not tested / proof gaps: no live Telegram bot/device send was run. The proof is intentionally scoped to the changed `sessions_send` runtime boundary: Telegram topic keys are resolved as threaded by the plugin-owned session conversation resolver and are rejected before any gateway dispatch.
